summary: AE + SE walked Apex Analytics through Redwood SDK quickstarts (Python & TypeScript), auth patterns (API key vs SSO), environment setup, and simple generation + embeddings flow. Discussed Dedicated vs Hosted, VPC/private deployment concerns, and Optimize suggestions for batching and quantization. Agreed next steps: pricing, security deep dive, and bench tests.
topics: Hosting modes: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private/VPC
transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-12-28 15:00 PST | Duration: 45m | Attendees: Sofia Patel (Redwood AE), Marcus Lee (Redwood SE), Rachel Kim (Apex CTO), Liam O'Neill (Lead Eng), Priya Desai (SRE)

[00:00] Sofia: hey everyone thanks for joining, happy holidays, we'll keep this to ~45 minutes. i'm sofia, AE on the account, marcus our SE will walk through the SDK quickstart.
[00:12] Rachel: great thanks, we appreciate it. we want to see the python and typescript flows and confirm auth and networking for our environment.
[00:20] Marcus: awesome, quick agenda, quickstart installs, auth patterns (api key/env var, service principal, sso notes), demo python snippet for generation, ts streaming example, and some notes on dedicated/private deployment and Optimize suggestions.
[00:35] Liam: sounds good. our main constraints: sub-100ms 1kqps targets for short prompts, data residency in eu-west, and SOC2 requirements from procurement.
[00:45] Marcus: noted. we'll call out relevant pieces.

[01:05] Marcus: ok first let's install the SDKs. Python pip install redwood-inference (note: transcription sometimes shows "red wood"), and for ts npm i @redwood/inference.
[01:20] Marcus: for python quickstart, set REDWOOD_API_KEY as env var. example: export REDWOOD_API_KEY=sk-xxx. we also support --api-key in the client init but env var is nicer for CI.
[01:35] Priya: do you support oauth / sso for service accounts? we'd rather not store keys long-term for private infra.
[01:45] Sofia: yes, for Dedicated and Private we support SSO provisioning + short-lived tokens via our IAM integration; for hosted API you can also integrate with your idp to mint scoped keys. we'll follow up with the exact flow in the security doc.

[02:10] Marcus: python example, i'll paste in the transcript, apologies for formatting:

    from redwood import RedwoodClient
    client = RedwoodClient(api_key=os.getenv('REDWOOD_API_KEY'))
    resp = client.generate(model='redwood-alpha-1', prompt='Summarize the following...')
    print(resp.text)

[02:40] Marcus: note on models: you can pin to a version e.g. redwood-alpha-1@v2026-12-01 to keep behavior stable.

[03:05] Rachel: what about streaming? our product streams partial tokens to users.
[03:12] Marcus: typescript example for streaming and function calling:

    import { Redwood } from '@redwood/inference'
    const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY })
    const stream = client.chat.stream({ model: 'redwood-chat-1', messages: [...] })
    for await (const chunk of stream) {
      // render partial token chunk
    }

[03:45] Marcus: we also support function/tool calling patterns, you can register handlers and the model will trigger them — good for structured outputs.

[04:05] Liam: any gotchas with node versions or bundlers? we run edge lambdas.
[04:12] Marcus: use node 18+, for edge runtimes we provide a lighter-weight fetch-based client and recommend using streaming through web sockets if you need low-latency tail. there are a few polyfills needed for older bundlers; i'll share the exact example repo.

[04:40] Rachel: auth again — for our VPC/private deployment we need KMS integration and audit logs. is that supported?
[04:50] Sofia: yes, Private supports customer-managed KMS/HSM and audit logs; Dedicated offers audit logs with an add-on. we'll attach the SOC2 + architecture whitepaper.

[05:10] Marcus: quick demo of batching and caching — Optimize suggests enabling prefix KV cache for chatbots with repeated prompts. that'll cut token cost significantly.
[05:25] Marcus: example: client.set_cache_policy({ prefix_kv: true, ttl_secs: 3600 }) — transcription may show as "K-V cash" sometimes.

[05:40] Priya: how does that interact with PII? if we cache user messages, we need redaction.
[05:48] Marcus: good point — Optimize can hint which prefixes are safe to cache; you can also set rules to hash or redact before caching. we'll share the docs for redaction + retention.

[06:10] Marcus: now switching to a short live demo — i'll run a small generate and stream back.
[06:20] [typing sounds]
[06:30] Marcus: starting a 1k token prompt to show latency — this is a contrived example, but more realistic is 50-150 token prompts for UI chat.
[06:40] Marcus: (stream) Hello — this part shows partial tokens being emitted.
[06:50] Rachel: looks good. what's the p99 on small prompts on Dedicated?
[06:56] Marcus: Dedicated with pinned model and tuned batching we see 50-120ms p50 and p99 depends on qps and packing, usually under 400ms for short prompts on T4/A10-style hardware; on xpu/advance cards lower. caveat: numbers vary a lot by model family and quantization.

[07:30] Liam: for our 1k qps target, how do you handle sharding and autoscale?
[07:38] Marcus: Dedicated supports reserved GPU pools with autoscale policies and burst capacity. smart routing will spill to compatible model variants if you run out of capacity. for strict SLOs we recommend reserved capacity + regional redundancy.

[08:05] Rachel: what's the difference between Dedicated and Private in terms of control?
[08:12] Sofia: Dedicated is Redwood-managed infra but isolated to your account (dedicated GPU pool). Private gives you the control plane in your VPC or on-prem with customer-managed networking and full KMS options. both support RBAC and audit logs.

[08:40] Marcus: back to SDK specifics — packaging, quickstart repo link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/quickstart (we'll send exact link, may be truncated here). contains python/, ts/ examples, and a small benchmark harness.

[09:05] Marcus: on the TS side, an example of function calling and structured json extraction — we demonstrate how to pass a schema and get direct data back.

[09:25] Priya: do you support streaming embeddings? we want to embed high volume docs and batch that.
[09:33] Marcus: embeddings are batched on the client; you can use the bulk embeddings endpoint with a csv or via the SDK batch helper. Optimize will suggest quantization for dense retrieval models and recommend batch sizes based on latency targets.

[10:00] Rachel: any rate limiting concerns? we have bursty traffic patterns.
[10:07] Sofia: yes, rate limits apply for hosted tiers; Dedicated gives you predictable throughput and quotas we can size for you. we also offer graceful degradation policies.

[10:25] Marcus: a few common pitfalls: 1) not pinning model versions — causes drift in outputs; 2) using too-large batch sizes for low-latency paths; 3) missing prefix cache configuration for chatbots.

[11:00] Liam: about model quantization — can you run 4-bit quantized models and what's the tradeoff?
[11:08] Marcus: we support multiple quantization profiles; 4-bit reduces memory and increases throughput with some quality tradeoffs. Optimize will recommend which quant profile to use per workload and provide regression testing harnesses so you can measure quality impact on your prompts.

[11:40] Rachel: procurement is asking for SOC2 and data residency proof. can you send the docs?
[11:48] Sofia: yes we'll attach SOC2 report, ISO notes, and clarify eu-west region availability and dedicated private endpoints for data residency.

[12:05] Marcus: quick note on logs and observability — Console gives token-level breakdowns, per-route dashboards, and tracing hooks. you can hook in your own datadog or splunk via the tracing exporter.

[12:30] Priya: curious about SDK telemetry; we don't want user PII to leak.

[12:37] Marcus: SDK can be configured to scrub PII before sending telemetry; defaults are conservative but we'll share config flags.

[12:55] Marcus: switching to a mini quickstart checklist for python:
    - pip install redwood-inference
    - export REDWOOD_API_KEY=sk-xxx
    - python quickstart.py (example does generation + embed)

[13:15] Marcus: quickstart.py includes a small bench harness that runs N requests and measures p50/p99 and token cost.

[13:30] Rachel: what's the best way to test Dedicated latency vs Hosted before committing?

[13:38] Sofia: we usually run a short pilot on Dedicated reserved capacity or provide a hosted performance bench with Replay + synthetic load. for a full piece, we can create a dedicated pilot environment for you.

[14:00] Liam: network topology — our infra sits behind corporate NATs and we use egress proxies. any special firewall rules?

[14:08] Marcus: outbound to Redwood endpoints on port 443; if using Private within the VPC we can keep traffic internal. we'll send the exact CIDR ranges and endpoint hostnames.

[14:30] Rachel: do you support on-prem air-gapped?

[14:35] Sofia: yes, Private has an on-prem package for air-gapped installs; that includes a different licensing agreement and support terms.

[15:00] Marcus: demo: run embedding batch (shows 200 docs batched) — results printed, slight lag for large batches but throughput is high.

[15:20] Marcus: note on cost controls: Console allows per-route token budgets and alerting. you can set thresholds and automatic fallback to smaller model variants.

[15:45] Priya: for the fallback, can we control model variants? we need strict quality for certain flows.

[15:52] Marcus: yes, you can pin routes to model families and set fallback chains; we support automatic regression alerts when a fallback changes quality.

[16:20] Sofia: wrapping up, agreed next steps: we'll send pricing + SOC2/security pack, marcus will push quickstart repos and example benchmarks, apex will run an initial bench and we'll schedule security deep dive.

[16:40] Rachel: perfect. anyone else have questions?

[16:45] Liam: nothing else. thanks both.

[16:50] Sofia: thanks all. meeting end.

Notes: transcript contains minor transcription errors (names, small code formatting). References: quickstart repo link (to be emailed), security pack link, pricing doc (to be emailed).
